summary: The root بَتَلَ (batala) means to cut off, sever, or separate something from another. It can also refer to making something obligatory, like a pilgrimage or a gift of a house for life.
lane: 1 بَتَلَهُ بتل بتله بتلة تل تلة , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. بَتِلَ , (S,) or بَتُلَ , (Msb,) or both, (M, K,) inf. n. بَتْلٌ , (Lth, T, S, &c.,) He cut it off, or severed it; (M, Msb, K;) as also , (M, K,) inf. n. تَبْتِيلٌ : (TA:) he separated it (Lth, T, S, M, Msb, K) from another thing. (Lth, T, S, M, K.) -b2- [Hence,] بَتَلَ العُمْرَةَ He made the performance of the عمرة [or minor pilgrimage ] to be obligatory, by itself. (A, TA.) And العُمْرَى He made the عمرى to be obligatory [upon himself ]; i. e., the saying, I have assigned to thee my house that thou mayest inhabit it to the end of my life. (TA.) -A2- بَتِلَ , aor. بَتَلَ , inf. n. بَتْلٌ , [but accord. to analogy, this should rather be بَتلٌ ,] He (a man) was, or became, wide between the shoulders. (T.)

headwords.def: بَتَلَهُ بتل بتله بتلة تل تلة, (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. بَتِلَ, (S,) or بَتُلَ, (Msb,) or both, (M, K,) inf. n. بَتْلٌ, (Lth, T, S, &c.,) He cut it off, or severed it; (M, Msb, K;) as also, (M, K,) inf. n. تَبْتِيلٌ: (TA:) he separated it (Lth, T, S, M, Msb, K) from another thing. (Lth, T, S, M, K.) [Hence,] بَتَلَ العُمْرَةَ He made the performance of the عمرة [or minor pilgrimage ] to be obligatory, by itself. (A, TA.) And العُمْرَى He made the عمرى to be obligatory [upon himself ]; i.
بَتَّلَ see 1, in two places: and see also 5: and مُبَتَّلٌ.

تبتّلا بتل تبتل تبتلا ٱبتل: see 7, in two places. [Hence,] He was, or became, alone. (TA.) Also, (S,) or تبتّلا إِلَى اللّٰهِ, (M, K,) and, (S, * K,) inf. n. تَبْتِيلٌ, (S,) He detached himself from worldly things, and devoted himself to God: (S:) or he devoted himself to God exclusively, and was sincere, or without hypocrisy, towards Him: (M, K:) he forsook every other thing, and applied himself to the service of God: (Fr, T:) he devoted himself exclusively to the service of God:…

انبتل أنبتل انبتل ٱنبتل It was, or became, cut off, or severed; (S, M, K;) as also. (M, K.) You say, انبتلت الفسِيلَةُ, (K, [in a copy of the M, probably a mistranscription,]) The shoot, or offset, of the palm-tree was cut off, or severed, مِنْ أُمِّهَا [ from its mother-tree ]; as also and. (M, K.) انبتل فِى سَيْرِهِ He strove, laboured, or exerted himself, and made much progress, in his journeying, or pace. (TA.)

عَطَآءٌ بَتْلٌ عطآء بتل A gift that is [ as it were ] cut off; i. e., of which there is not the like; or after which another is not given. (M, K.) And صَدَقَةٌ بَتْلَةٌ, (M, K,) and صدقة بَتَّةٌ بَتْلَةٌ, (TA,) An alms, or a gift for the sake of God, cut off from its giver: (M, K:) or cut off from all the property [ irrevocably ], to be devoted to the cause of God. (O, TA. [See also art. بت.]) You say also, أَعْطَيْتُهُ هٰ ِهِ العَطِيَّةَ بَتَّا بَتْلًا: see art. بت.

بَتُولٌ بتول تولي A shoot, or an offset, of a palm-tree, cut off from its mother-tree, and independent thereof; as also, (As, T, S, M, K,) and. (M, K.) A virgin, that is cut off from husbands: (S:) a woman that withholds herself from men, (T,) or that is cut off from men, (M, K,) having no desire for them, (T, M, TA,) nor need of them; (T;) and, with the art. ال, applied to the Virgin Mary; (M, K;) as also: (M, K:) with the art.

بَتِيلٌ بتيل: see بَتُولٌ, in three places. Also Slender; (Ham p. 589;) applied to a waist; (Ham, TA;) as also. (TA.) A tree having its racemes pendulous. (K. [See also مُبْتِلٌ.]) A watercourse (Ibn-'Abbád, M, K) in the lower part of a valley: pl. بُتُلٌ. (M, K.)

بَتِيلَةٌ بتيله بتيلة: see بَتُولٌ, in two places. Also Any limb, or member, (Lth, T, S, M, K,) with its flesh, (Lth, T, S,) separate from others, (M, K,) or by itself: (Lth, T:) pl. بَتَائِلُ. (Lth, T, S, &c.) In one dial., (M,) The posteriors; (M, K;) because divided [or distinct] from the back. (M.) مَرَّ عَلَى بَتِيلَةٍ مِنْ رَأْيِهِ, and من رأيه, [ He proceeded according to] an irrevocable determination or resolution. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.)
; fem. بَتْلَآءُ: for the latter, see what next precedes. عُمْرَةٌ بَتْلَآءُ [ A minor pilgrimage] not conjoined with another. (K.) And أَبْتَلُ, applied to a man, Wide between the shoulders. (T.)

مُبْتِلٌ مبتل مبتلي, (As, T, S,) or مُبْتِلَةٌ, (M, K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, مُبْتَلَة,]) the first being [in the opinion of ISd] pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.] of the second, like as تَمْرٌ is of تَمرَةٌ, (M,) A palmtree ( نَخْلَةٌ ) having a shoot, or an offset, cut off from it and independent of it; (As, T, S, M, K;) and used in like manner as a pl.; i.

مُبَتَّلٌ مبتل مبتلي: see بَتيِلٌ. مُبَتَّلَةٌ, applied to a woman, Beautiful, elegant, or pretty; (K;) as though her beauty were divided into portions (, i. e. قُطِّعَ,) [ and distributed in due proportions ] upon her limbs: (M, * K:) or perfect in make, (S,) whose flesh is not accumulated, one portion upon another, (S, M, K,) but distinctly disposed; this latter being said by some to be the meaning: (M:) or, accord.
مُنْبَتِلٌ منبتل Cut off, or severed. (S.) [And hence,] عَزِيمَةٌ مُنْبَتِلَةٌ An irrevocable determination or resolution. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
